titre: Low voltage safety file and CE
autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
citation: Where compliance of electrical equipment with the safety objectives referred to in Article 3 and set out in Annex I has been demonstrated by the conformity assessment procedure referred to in the first subparagraph, manufacturers shall draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking.
exigence: Once the conformity assessment has shown compliance with the safety objectives, the manufacturer must draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking.
note: Article 6(2), first subparagraph: the manufacturer draws up the technical documentation of Annex III and carries out the conformity assessment. Scope read in Article 1: equipment rated between 50 and 1 000 V AC and between 75 and 1 500 V DC. The charger (input 100-240 V AC) is inside these limits. The laptop input is 20 V DC, below the 75 V DC limit, so its safety is handled through the radio equipment directive (see eu-red-exigences). Article 6(3): documentation and declaration kept 10 years. Article 8: the importer checks all this before placing on the market.

autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
citation: Manufacturers shall draw up the technical documentation referred to in Annex II or Annex III and carry out the relevant conformity assessment procedure referred to in Article 14 or have it carried out. Where compliance of apparatus with the applicable requirements has been demonstrated by that procedure, manufacturers shall draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking.
exigence: The manufacturer must draw up the EMC technical documentation, carry out the conformity assessment, draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking.
note: Listed for the charger only. Article 2(2)(a) of the text as published excludes equipment covered by Directive 1999/5/EC (the former radio equipment directive); for the laptop, EMC is an essential requirement of Directive 2014/53/EU (see eu-red-exigences).

autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
citation: Radio equipment shall be constructed so as to ensure: (a) the protection of health and safety of persons and of domestic animals and the protection of property, including the objectives with respect to safety requirements set out in Directive 2014/35/EU, but with no voltage limit applying; (b) an adequate level of electromagnetic compatibility as set out in Directive 2014/30/EU.
exigence: The laptop, as radio equipment, must be built to meet the safety objectives of the low voltage directive with no voltage limit and an adequate level of electromagnetic compatibility.
note: The laptop contains a Wi-Fi/Bluetooth module, so it is radio equipment. Quoted from the text as originally published; Article 3(1) is unchanged in the consolidated version of 28.12.2024, which was also read. Article 3(2) adds efficient use of radio spectrum. Article 10(3): the manufacturer draws up the technical documentation, carries out the conformity assessment, draws up an EU declaration of conformity and affixes the CE marking; Article 10(4): kept 10 years.

autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
article: Annex (new Annex Ia to Directive 2014/53/EU), Part I, points 1.13 and 2.1
citation: 1.13. laptops. 2. In so far as they are capable of being recharged by means of wired charging, the categories or classes of radio equipment referred to in point 1 of this Part shall: 2.1. be equipped with the USB Type-C receptacle
exigence: A laptop that can be recharged by wired charging must be equipped with a USB Type-C receptacle.
note: Article 2(1) of Directive (EU) 2022/2380: Member States apply the rules from 28 December 2024 for points 1.1 to 1.12 and from 28 April 2026 for point 1.13 (laptops). The consolidated version of Directive 2014/53/EU dated 28.12.2024 still lists only points 1.1 to 1.12, which is why the amending directive is quoted. Part I point 3 (read in the consolidated text): above 5 V, 3 A or 15 W the equipment must incorporate USB Power Delivery; the laptop label shows a 20 V 3.4 A input. Article 3a: the buyer must be offered the equipment without a charging device, with a pictogram on the packaging and, for distance selling, close to the price. The label does not show the connector type, so the port itself was not checked. This directive regulates the radio equipment, not a charger sold alone.

autorite: European Commission; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
citation: 1. Energy efficiency requirements: (a) from 1 April 2020, the no-load condition power consumption shall not exceed the following values:
exigence: The charger must stay within the no-load power consumption limit set in Annex II, which also sets a minimum average active efficiency and nameplate information.
note: Scope read in Article 2(1): nameplate output power not exceeding 250 watts, used with the equipment of Annex I (which lists information technology equipment). A 70 W adapter is inside that limit. Values read in Annex II for an AC-DC supply above 49,0 W that is neither low voltage nor multiple voltage output: no-load 0,21 W, average active efficiency not less than 0,880; whether this adapter falls in the low voltage class of Article 2(2) was not determined. This is the regulation in application today: Regulation (EU) 2025/2052 repeals it with effect from 14 December 2028.

acte: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2052 (ecodesign, external power supplies and chargers)
autorite: European Commission; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
citation: An AC-DC EPS shall be an interoperable EPS that meets all the requirements set out in point (b) unless it fulfils the requirements set out in point (c). (b) An interoperable EPS shall satisfy all the following requirements: (1) it shall be fitted with at least one USB Type-C or USB-PD port;
exigence: From the date of application, an AC-DC external power supply must be interoperable, which includes at least one USB Type-C or USB-PD port, unless an exemption of point 3(c) applies.
note: Not yet in application: Article 10 says the regulation applies from 14 December 2028, and Article 8 repeals Regulation (EU) 2019/1782 from the same date. Article 9(3), applicable from 14 December 2025: a supply placed on the market between 14 December 2025 and 14 December 2028 that meets this regulation is considered to comply with Regulation (EU) 2019/1782. Point 3(c) exempts, among others, supplies with a nameplate output power greater than 100 W; a 70 W adapter is below that limit. The new definition (Article 2(1)) no longer has the 250 W ceiling and covers supplies sold with or without the powered product. Annex III defines a common charger logo.

acte: Commission Regulation (EU) No 617/2013 (ecodesign, computers and computer servers)
autorite: European Commission; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
citation: The ecodesign requirements for computers and computer servers are set out in Annex II. Compliance of computers and computer servers with the applicable ecodesign requirements shall be measured in accordance with the methods set out in Annex III.
exigence: The laptop must meet the ecodesign requirements of Annex II, measured with the methods of Annex III.
note: Article 1(2)(c) lists notebook computers among the products covered. Dates read in the final article: most points of Annex II apply from 1 July 2014, points 1.2 and 1.4 from 1 January 2016. Text read as originally published; later amendments were not read.

autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
citation: manufacturers draw up the required technical documentation and carry out the internal production control procedure in line with module A of Annex II to Decision No 768/2008/EC or have it carried out; (c) where compliance of EEE with the applicable requirements has been demonstrated by the procedure referred to in point (b), manufacturers draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking on the finished product.
exigence: The manufacturer must draw up the technical documentation, carry out internal production control, draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking.
note: Article 7(a) requires design and manufacture in accordance with Article 4, which bans the substances of Annex II above the stated concentrations. Annex I category 3 is IT and telecommunications equipment. The original Annex II read here lists six substances (lead, mercury, hexavalent chromium, PBB, PBDE at 0,1 %, cadmium at 0,01 %); the annex has been amended since and the consolidated list was not read in this task.

autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
citation: With a view to minimising the disposal of WEEE as unsorted municipal waste and to facilitating its separate collection, Member States shall ensure that producers appropriately mark — preferably in accordance with the European standard EN 50419 ( 25 ) — EEE placed on the market with the symbol shown in Annex IX.
exigence: The producer must mark the equipment with the crossed-out wheeled bin symbol of Annex IX.
note: The characters ( 25 ) in the quote are the footnote reference of the official text. Annex IX: the symbol must be printed visibly, legibly and indelibly. This is a directive: the obligation is carried by each national transposition, which was not read.

autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
citation: Producers supplying EEE by means of distance communication as defined in Article 3(1)(f)(iv) shall be registered in the Member State that they sell to. Where such producers are not registered in the Member State that they are selling to, they shall be registered through their authorised representatives as referred to in Article 17(2).
exigence: A seller supplying equipment by distance communication must be registered as a producer in each Member State it sells to, directly or through an authorised representative.
note: Article 3(1)(f)(iv) defines as producer anyone who sells by distance communication directly to households in a Member State and is established in another Member State or in a third country. Article 12: producers finance collection and treatment of household WEEE. Registers, fees and take-back schemes are national (France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Netherlands each have their own); the national texts were not read.

autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
citation: From 18 August 2025, all batteries shall be marked with the symbol for separate collection of batteries (‘separate collection symbol’) as shown in Part B of Annex VI.
exigence: The battery inside the laptop must carry the separate collection symbol.
note: Article 1(3): the regulation also applies to batteries incorporated into products. The symbol seen is on the laptop label; the battery itself was not photographed. Other points read: Article 38, the battery manufacturer draws up technical documentation, an EU declaration of conformity and affixes the CE marking; Article 13(6), QR code from 18 February 2027; Article 11, portable batteries removable and replaceable by the end-user, applicable from 18 February 2027; Article 55(2), producers must be registered in each Member State where they make batteries available, including batteries incorporated in appliances (Chapter VIII applies from 18 August 2025).

autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
citation: Where economic operators make products available on the market online or through other means of distance sales, the offer of those products shall clearly and visibly indicate at least the following information: (a) name, registered trade name or registered trade mark of the manufacturer, as well as the postal and electronic address at which they can be contacted;
exigence: Each online offer must clearly and visibly show the name of the manufacturer and the postal and electronic address at which it can be contacted.
note: Article 19(b): where the manufacturer is not established in the Union, the offer must also show the name, postal and electronic address of the responsible person within the meaning of Article 16(1) of this regulation or Article 4(1) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020. Points (c) and (d): product identification with a picture, and warnings in a language consumers understand. Scope limit read in Article 2(1): for products covered by Union harmonisation legislation, Chapter III Section 1 (which contains Article 16) does not apply, so the responsible person for these two products comes from Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 (see eu-operateur-responsable); Article 19 sits in Section 2.

titre: Economic operator established in the Union
acte: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 (market surveillance and compliance of products)
autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
citation: Notwithstanding any obligations set out in applicable Union harmonisation legislation, a product subject to legislation referred to in paragraph 5 may be placed on the market only if there is an economic operator established in the Union who is responsible for the tasks set out in paragraph 3 in respect of that product.
exigence: The seller must have an economic operator established in the Union responsible for the tasks of Article 4(3) before the product is placed on the market.
note: Article 4(2): that operator is the EU manufacturer, the importer, an authorised representative with a written mandate, or failing those the fulfilment service provider established in the Union. Article 4(4): its name and contact details including postal address must be on the product, its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document. Article 4(5) lists the legislation concerned, including Directives 2009/125/EC, 2011/65/EU, 2014/30/EU, 2014/35/EU and 2014/53/EU.

acte: Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 (accreditation and market surveillance, CE marking)
autorite: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; enforced by national market surveillance authorities
citation: By affixing or having affixed the CE marking, the manufacturer indicates that he takes responsibility for the conformity of the product with all applicable requirements set out in the relevant Community harmonisation legislation providing for its affixing.
exigence: The manufacturer who affixes the CE marking takes responsibility for conformity with every requirement of the legislation that provides for it.
note: Article 30(1): only the manufacturer or its authorised representative may affix the CE marking. Article 30(5): no marking likely to mislead about the meaning or form of the CE marking. For these products the CE marking is provided for by the acts listed in the other EU entries.

autorite: Secretary of State (UK)
citation: Before placing electrical equipment on the market, a manufacturer must ensure that it has been designed and manufactured in accordance with the principal elements of the safety objectives.
exigence: The manufacturer must ensure the charger is designed and manufactured in accordance with the principal elements of the safety objectives.
note: Regulation 3: applies to equipment rated between 50 and 1000 V AC and between 75 and 1500 V DC. Regulation 6(1): declaration of conformity and UK marking before placing on the market. No UKCA mark is in the list of marks seen on the charger; see gb-marquage-ce-reconnu for the CE route. Enforcement body not read in this task.

titre: CE marking accepted in Great Britain
autorite: Secretary of State (UK)
citation: any reference to “UK marking” is to be read as a reference to the CE marking;
exigence: Where the manufacturer uses the EU directive route of regulation 34A, the references to the UK marking in the regulations are read as references to the CE marking.
note: Regulation 34A (title: Obligations which are met by complying with obligations in the Directive) extends to England, Wales and Scotland. Paragraph (2) sets the conditions: design to Annex I of the Directive, conformity assessment under Annex III, technical documentation, records in English, CE marking affixed, and an EU declaration of conformity in English. Paragraph (3)(a): regulations 4, 5, 6(1) and (3) are then treated as satisfied. The quote is short because each quote must sit inside one paragraph of the official page. Paragraph (4): the importer must ensure the equipment bears the CE marking. The Radio Equipment Regulations 2017 (regulation 36A) and the Electromagnetic Compatibility Regulations 2016 (regulation 38A) have a provision with the same title in their table of contents; their bodies were not read.

autorite: Secretary of State (UK)
citation: Before placing radio equipment on the market, a manufacturer must ensure that it has been designed and manufactured in accordance with the essential requirements.
exigence: The manufacturer must ensure the laptop, as radio equipment, is designed and manufactured in accordance with the essential requirements.
note: Regulation 6(1): the essential requirements include health and safety by reference to the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 and an adequate level of electromagnetic compatibility. Regulation 10(1): declaration of conformity and UK marking before placing on the market. No USB-C common charger requirement was found in the provisions read for Great Britain.

acte: The Restriction of the Use of Certain Hazardous Substances in Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2012 (S.I. 2012/3032)
autorite: Secretary of State (UK)
citation: A manufacturer must not place EEE on the market unless the EEE complies with the requirements of regulation 3 (restriction on the use of certain hazardous substances in EEE).
exigence: The manufacturer must not place the equipment on the market unless it respects the substance restrictions of regulation 3.
note: Regulation 3 (England, Wales and Scotland version): equipment must not contain the substances listed in Schedule A1 above the maximum concentration values. Regulation 10(2) and regulation 16: technical documentation, declaration of conformity and UK marking. UKCA is in the list of marks seen on the laptop but not on the charger. The contents of Schedule A1 were not read.

titre: Crossed out bin symbol in UK
acte: The Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013 (S.I. 2013/3113)
autorite: Secretary of State (UK)
citation: Except where paragraph (3) applies, the crossed out wheeled bin symbol [ F2 must ] be affixed in a visible, legible and indelible form to each item of equipment.
exigence: Each item of equipment must carry the crossed out wheeled bin symbol in a visible, legible and indelible form.

Regulation 22(1): the duty falls on the producer or authorised representative who places the equipment on the market. Regulation 14(1A) and (2), also read: a non-UK supplier supplying EEE directly to private households or other users in the United Kingdom must either appoint an authorised representative established in the United Kingdom or be a member of a compliance scheme itself.

acte: Ordonnance sur les matériels électriques à basse tension (OMBT), RS 734.26
autorite: Conseil fédéral suisse; Inspection fédérale des installations à courant fort (ESTI)
citation: L’obligation d’apposer le marquage «CE» ne s’applique pas. Si le marquage «CE» est déjà apposé en conformité avec les prescriptions de l’UE sur des matériels selon l’art. 1, al. 1, il n’est pas nécessaire de l’enlever.
exigence: The CE marking is not required in Switzerland for low voltage equipment and may stay on the charger if it was affixed in line with EU rules.
note: No English version on Fedlex, quote in French. Art. 8 al. 1: any economic operator making the equipment available must be able to present a declaration of conformity; Art. 8 al. 4: in a Swiss official language or in English, and conformity with EU law may be declared under Annex IV of the EU low voltage directive. Art. 4 al. 1: operator obligations follow Articles 6 to 9 of Directive 2014/35/EU. Art. 1: same voltage limits as the EU (50 V to 1000 V AC, 75 V to 1500 V DC). Art. 6 al. 2: if the manufacturer is not in Switzerland, has no representative and there is no importer, the fulfilment service provider must be named on the equipment, packaging or documents.

autorite: Swiss Federal Council; Federal Office of Communications (OFCOM)
citation: Each apparatus must bear the conformity marking in accordance with Annex 1 point 1 or the foreign conformity marking in accordance with Annex 1 point 2.
exigence: The charger must bear either the Swiss conformity marking or the foreign conformity marking of Annex 1 point 2.
note: Annex 1 point 2.1: the conformity marking of Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 (the CE marking) is permitted. Art. 12: the manufacturer, its authorised representative or, if neither is established in Switzerland, the importer must be able to produce the declaration of conformity and technical documentation for ten years. Art. 4 sets the essential requirements. English translation published by Fedlex, stated there to have no legal force.

autorite: Swiss Federal Council; Federal Office of Communications (OFCOM)
citation: All radio equipment must bear the conformity marking in accordance with Annex 1 number 1 or the foreign conformity marking in accordance with Annex 1 number 2.
exigence: The laptop must bear either the Swiss conformity marking or the foreign conformity marking of Annex 1 number 2.
note: Annex 1 point 2.1: the conformity marking of Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 (the CE marking) is permitted. Art. 7 para. 1: safety by reference to the low voltage ordinance with no voltage limit, and electromagnetic compatibility. Art. 7 para. 2bis: radio equipment that can be charged by cable and is widely available must be capable of being charged using a USB-C connection, for the categories defined by OFCOM; the OFCOM provisions were not read, so it is not established here whether laptops are in those categories. English translation published by Fedlex, stated there to have no legal force.

acte: Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance (ORRChem), SR 814.81, Annex 2.18
autorite: Swiss Federal Council; Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN)
citation: Without prejudice to Numbers 3 and 8, the manufacturer placing electrical and electronic equipment on the market must ensure that it has been designed and manufactured in accordance with the requirements specified in Number 2.
exigence: The manufacturer must ensure the equipment is designed and manufactured within the substance limits of Annex 2.18 number 2.
note: Number 2 para. 1 lists ten substances with maximum concentrations in homogeneous material: lead, mercury, hexavalent chromium, PBB, PBDE, DEHP, BBP, DBP and DIBP at 0.1 %, cadmium at 0.01 %. Number 4.1 para. 2: technical documentation and internal production control. Annex 2.15 of the same ordinance covers batteries: number 4.1 requires separate collection information on batteries, including for manufacturers of appliances containing batteries. Version in force on 16 July 2026. English translation published by Fedlex, stated there to have no legal force.

acte: Ordonnance sur les exigences relatives à l’efficacité énergétique (OEEE), RS 730.02, annexe 2.2
autorite: Conseil fédéral suisse; Office fédéral de l’énergie (OFEN)
citation: Les sources d’alimentation visées au ch. 1 peuvent être mises en circulation ou fournies si elles satisfont aux exigences visées à l’art. 3 et à l’annexe II du règlement (UE) 2019/1782.
exigence: The charger may be placed on the Swiss market only if it meets Article 3 and Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2019/1782.
note: No English version on Fedlex, quote in French. Annexe 2.2 ch. 1.1 and 1.3: scope and definitions are those of Regulation (EU) 2019/1782, so the 250 W limit of the EU text applies. Version of the ordinance in force on 24 July 2026; it still refers to Regulation (EU) 2019/1782. The authority named for enforcement was not read in the text.

acte: Ordonnance sur les exigences relatives à l’efficacité énergétique (OEEE), RS 730.02, annexe 2.3
autorite: Conseil fédéral suisse; Office fédéral de l’énergie (OFEN)
citation: Les ordinateurs visés au ch. 1 peuvent être mis en circulation ou fournis s’ils remplissent les exigences fixées à l’art. 3 et à l’annexe II du règlement (UE) n o 617/2013 pour le type d’appareil correspondant.
exigence: The laptop may be placed on the Swiss market only if it meets Article 3 and Annex II of Regulation (EU) No 617/2013 for its type.
note: No English version on Fedlex, quote in French. Annexe 2.3 ch. 1.1: covers the computers listed in Article 1(2) of Regulation (EU) No 617/2013, which includes notebook computers. The authority named for enforcement was not read in the text.
